proposal: The Mandate recommends moving Title I, Part A to HHS's Administration for Children and Families as a no-strings formula block grant with revenue responsibility returned to states over 10 years, and converting most IDEA funding to a no-strings block grant distributed through HHS's Administration for Community Living. It also floats small education savings accounts for IDEA and Title I families and state opt-outs from federal ESEA programs.
remaining: Legislation converting Title I to a no-strings formula block grant under HHS's Administration for Children and Families: none found; the FY2027 request keeps Title I Part A as a formula program at 18.4 billion dollars.
A 10-year phase-out of federal Title I funding with states assuming revenue responsibility: no proposal found in the sources reviewed.

Converting most IDEA funding to a block grant under HHS's Administration for Community Living: not found; the FY2027 request increases IDEA state grants, and the HHS component for the special education move was not named in the sources.

Small education savings accounts for IDEA and Title I families and state opt-outs from ESEA programs (APLUS-style): not found; the proposed MEGA block grant consolidates 17 other programs but does not provide per-child accounts or opt-outs.

status_summary: As of 2026-10-07 administration of these programs is moving away from ED's day-to-day management, but their funding structure is unchanged and the administration's FY2027 request keeps Title I and IDEA as formula programs. Under an ED and DOL interagency agreement signed on 2025-09-30 and announced on 2025-11-18, Labor provides administrative support for about 42 elementary and secondary program services, including Title I, Part A, while ED keeps statutory authority (the Mandate named HHS, not Labor), and a 2026-06-16 agreement shifts day-to-day management of OSERS, which runs IDEA, to HHS; OSERS staff began moving into HHS space in early September 2026, while ED retains statutory responsibility and IDEA funds continue to flow through ED. The FY2027 budget document (April 2026) keeps Title I at $18.4 billion, raises IDEA State Grants by $489 million while folding in six smaller IDEA programs, and requests $2 billion for a Make Education Great Again grant that consolidates 17 other K-12 programs (the budget text describes it as a consolidation giving states more flexibility, which AASA calls a state block grant), so consolidation is proposed for other programs but not for Title I or IDEA, and the Education section proposes no transfers to HHS, though it proposes moving Career and Technical Education to Labor. No Title I phase-out, IDEA block grant or per-child account was found, and Congress funded ED in FY2026 and rejected the requested cut and program moves, per Federal News Network.

timeline.event: ED and DOL sign the Elementary and Secondary Education Partnership interagency agreement, which lists Title I, Part A among the program services DOL's Employment and Training Administration supports; ED retains statutory authority and OESE management. Announced 2025-11-18.

The Departments of Labor and Education announce interagency agreements (DOL release 25-1512-NAT): an Elementary and Secondary Education Partnership under which Labor takes a greater role in administering federal K-12 programs (managing competitions, providing technical assistance and folding programs into employment and training programs) and a Postsecondary Education Partnership for most Higher Education Act grant programs, both with oversight by the Education Department. The Labor release does not name Title I; K-12 Dive reports that Title I and other Office of Elementary and Secondary Education programs are assigned to Labor.

FY2026 appropriations for ED are enacted (Pub. L. 119-75, per a coalition letter of 2026-09-30). Federal News Network reports Congress rejected the requested $12 billion cut and the proposal to move core programs.

AASA summarizes the FY2027 request: Title I Part A level-funded at 18.4 billion dollars, IDEA increased, and a Make Education Great Again grant program consolidating 17 programs worth 6.5 billion dollars into a 2 billion dollar grant; neither Title I nor IDEA is described as block-granted or phased out. NAESP (2026-04-16) reports IDEA state grants of 15.4 billion dollars, a net increase of 522 million.

The President's FY2027 Budget (document posted under an April 2026 path; the date is that of AASA's summary) requests $76.5 billion in discretionary budget authority for the Department of Education (down $2.3 billion, 2.9 percent, from 2026); keeps Title I at $18.4 billion; raises IDEA State Grants by $489 million while folding six smaller IDEA programs into them (total IDEA about $16 billion); requests $2 billion for a new 'Make Education Great Again' (MEGA) grant consolidating 17 programs totaling $6.5 billion, eliminates 12 other programs totaling $2.1 billion, and sends Career and Technical Education to Labor. The Education section proposes no transfers to HHS and does not block grant Title I or IDEA; it describes MEGA as a consolidation that gives states more flexibility.

ED announces an agreement under which HHS takes over day-to-day management of OSERS and IDEA programs. ED keeps statutory responsibility and enforcement authority; funding continues through ED for now.

House Education and Workforce Committee Republicans release a ten-bill package; H.R. 9610 would transfer elementary and secondary programs, including Title I, to Labor. The reporting does not mention block grants, and it does not mention IDEA.
timeline.source: Daily Signal (posted by House Education and Workforce Committee)

timeline.event: Senate HELP Committee advances S. 5046 (13-9), led by Sen. Kaine with Sens. Collins and Murkowski, which would prohibit transfers of programs from four ED offices including OSERS and the elementary and secondary office. Committee Chairman Cassidy opposed the bill and opposes moving special education to HHS.

Government Executive reports ED began moving some employees into other agencies' buildings the previous week, with OSERS to HHS and the elementary and secondary office to Labor under 14 interagency agreements.

title: Convert Title I and IDEA to no-strings block grants under HHS; phase out Title I
uncertainties: The ED and DOL agreement and the ED release of 2026-06-16 were read on ed.gov; the FY2027 budget Education pages were read in an earlier pass through a tool summary. The ED and HHS agreement text could not be fetched, and the ED release names special education and rehabilitative services but not OSERS or IDEA, so the OSERS and IDEA specifics and the HHS component rest on AASA, K-12 Dive and Government Executive. The budget's IDEA State Grants increase of $489 million differs from AASA's 1.167 billion dollars and NAESP's 522 million net figure, which use different framings and were not reconciled. The ED congressional justification was not read. The FY2026 enacted Title I and IDEA amounts were not retrieved; the 2026-02-03 enactment date comes from a coalition letter citing Pub. L. 119-75. The statement that no block-grant proposal for Title I or IDEA exists rests on absence of evidence in these sources. No Federal Register notice of the agreements was found.
